simple_def: Putting aside a fixed amount of money every month into an investment.
intermediate_def: An automated discipline using rupee-cost averaging to buy mutual fund units regularly regardless of market ups and downs.
analogy: Like subscribing to Netflix, but instead of streaming shows, you're slowly buying pieces of India's biggest companies.

simple_def: A basket of many stocks or bonds managed by a professional.
intermediate_def: An investment vehicle that pools money from many investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of securities overseen by a SEBI-registered fund manager.
analogy: Instead of buying 50 individual groceries yourself, you buy a pre-packed curated meal kit with everything balanced.

simple_def: A low-cost fund that simply copies a major market index like NIFTY 50.
intermediate_def: A passively managed mutual fund that mirrors the composition and performance of a benchmark index with very low expense ratios.
analogy: Betting on the entire cricket team to score runs rather than betting on only one batsman.

simple_def: Money kept safely aside solely for unexpected crises like medical bills or job loss.
intermediate_def: Liquid savings covering 3 to 6 months of mandatory living expenses kept in high-liquidity instruments like savings accounts or liquid funds.
analogy: The spare tire in your car: you hope you never need it, but you never drive without it.

simple_def: Prices rising over time, making your money buy less year after year.
intermediate_def: The sustained percentage increase in the general price level of goods and services over time, measured in India by CPI.
analogy: A silent thief stealing 6% of the snacks out of your grocery bag every single year.

simple_def: Earning returns on your money, and then earning returns on those returns.
intermediate_def: The exponential mathematical process where accumulated interest or capital gains generate additional earnings over extended periods.
analogy: Rolling a small snowball down a long snowy mountain until it becomes an unstoppable boulder.

simple_def: Locking your money with a bank for a fixed duration to earn guaranteed interest.
intermediate_def: A low-risk financial instrument provided by banks offering higher fixed interest than regular savings accounts, insured up to ₹5 lakh by DICGC.
analogy: Renting out a room to a reliable tenant who promises a fixed rent every month on the dot.

simple_def: Depositing a fixed amount every month into a bank for guaranteed interest.
intermediate_def: A disciplined monthly savings product with a bank offering fixed tenure and guaranteed returns.
analogy: A digital piggy bank that rewards you with bonus pocket money for feeding it every month.

simple_def: A government-backed 15-year savings scheme with tax-free returns.
intermediate_def: A long-term sovereign statutory debt scheme eligible for EEE (exempt-exempt-exempt) tax treatment under Section 80C.
analogy: A safe locked vault sponsored by the government that keeps your retirement gold untaxed.

simple_def: A government-regulated retirement scheme that mixes equity and debt.
intermediate_def: A market-linked voluntary contribution pension system regulated by PFRDA with low fund management fees and additional tax deductions under 80CCD.
analogy: Planting a mango tree today so you can sit in its cool shade and eat fruit when you are 60.

simple_def: Government securities denominated in grams of gold instead of physical metal.
intermediate_def: RBI-issued government debt tracking the market price of 999 purity gold plus an annual 2.5% coupon, with capital gains tax exemption if held to maturity.
analogy: Owning digital gold with zero locker rent and getting paid interest just for holding it.

simple_def: Tax-saving mutual funds with a 3-year lock-in period.
intermediate_def: Equity mutual funds qualifying for Section 80C tax deduction with the shortest lock-in period (3 years) among tax-saving avenues.
analogy: A gym membership with a 3-year commitment that builds financial muscle while cutting your tax bill.

simple_def: The watchdog referee protecting investors in India's stock market.
intermediate_def: The Securities and Exchange Board of India: the statutory regulator established to protect retail investors and regulate financial markets.
analogy: The strict football referee who shows red cards and blows the whistle whenever players cheat.

simple_def: The annual percentage fee a mutual fund charges to manage your money.
intermediate_def: The operational cost ratio deducted daily from the fund’s Net Asset Value (NAV) covering management fees, administrative, and distribution costs.
analogy: The small entry ticket fee the amusement park deducts from your wallet every year.

simple_def: Not putting all your eggs in one basket.
intermediate_def: A risk management strategy that mixes a wide variety of uncorrelated investments within a portfolio to reduce unsystematic risk.
analogy: Carrying an umbrella, sunscreen, and a jacket on a hill station trip so no weather ruins your day.

simple_def: Buying more shares when prices drop and fewer when prices rise automatically.
intermediate_def: An investment strategy where an investor divides up the total amount to be invested across periodic purchases to reduce volatility impact.
analogy: Buying mangoes every month: when they are cheap you get a big carton, when expensive you get a few.

simple_def: A market condition where stock prices are rising and optimism is high.
intermediate_def: A sustained upward trend in financial markets accompanied by strong investor confidence and economic expansion.
analogy: A raging bull charging forward and thrusting its horns upward into the air.

simple_def: A market condition where prices drop 20% or more from recent peaks.
intermediate_def: A prolonged period of falling asset prices accompanied by widespread pessimism and panic selling.
analogy: A sleeping or attacking bear swiping its sharp paws downward.

simple_def: How quickly you can convert an asset into spendable cash without losing value.
intermediate_def: The ease and speed with which a security can be bought or sold in the market without substantially impacting its asset price.
analogy: Cash in your pocket flows like water; property is like concrete that takes months to set and move.

simple_def: Mutual funds that lend money to governments and corporations for interest.
intermediate_def: Fixed income mutual funds that invest in treasury bills, government securities, commercial paper, and corporate bonds.
analogy: Being the moneylender who collects steady interest rather than a partner sharing company profits.

simple_def: Mutual funds that buy shares of companies to participate in their growth.
intermediate_def: Funds investing at least 65% of assets in company shares, offering higher long-term growth with higher short-term fluctuations.
analogy: Owning a percentage of your local bakery: if it opens 10 branches, you get wealthy.

simple_def: Tax paid to the government on the profit made when selling an investment.
intermediate_def: Taxes levied on capital appreciation, split in India into Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) and Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG).
analogy: Giving a slice of your birthday cake to the house owner before taking the rest home.

simple_def: A cash share of company profits paid directly to shareholders.
intermediate_def: A distribution of a portion of a company's earnings decided by the board of directors to a class of its shareholders.
analogy: A fruit tree dropping ripe fruit into your basket while keeping the tree alive and standing.

simple_def: A scam that pays early members using money collected from newer recruits.
intermediate_def: A fraudulent investment operation that generates pseudo-returns for older investors through revenue paid by new investors rather than genuine legitimate profit.
analogy: Borrowing money from Ramesh to pay back Suresh, until you run out of people and vanish.

simple_def: Social media creators talking about money, stocks, and crypto.
intermediate_def: Online influencers sharing financial opinions, sometimes unregistered and paid by dubious apps to promote high-risk or fraudulent schemes.
analogy: A roadside megaphone seller claiming a magic tonic cures all diseases without a doctor's degree.

simple_def: A 3-digit score (300-900) showing banks how reliably you pay back debts.
intermediate_def: A numeric summary of your credit history calculated from credit card and loan repayment track records.
analogy: Your school report card, but for how responsibly you repay borrowed money.

simple_def: An electronic digital account that holds your shares and bonds safely.
intermediate_def: A dematerialized account operated through depositories (NSDL or CDSL) to hold securities electronically.
analogy: A digital locker where your share certificates are stored safely without risk of paper loss.

simple_def: The mandatory identity verification process required by financial institutions.
intermediate_def: A regulatory standard using PAN, Aadhaar, and bank verification to prevent money laundering and fraud.
analogy: Showing your student ID card or passport before entering an exam hall.

simple_def: Pure insurance that pays your family a large lump sum if you pass away.
intermediate_def: Low-cost high-coverage pure protection insurance without any investment return element.
analogy: An umbrella you carry only for heavy rain; you don't expect the umbrella to pay you if the sky stays sunny.

simple_def: How much investors are willing to pay for each ₹1 of company profit.
intermediate_def: Price-to-Earnings valuation ratio calculated by dividing the current share price by earnings per share (EPS).
analogy: Comparing how many months of rent you must pay up-front to buy a small chai stall.
